title: Load-balancing loss
goal:
Without a pressure toward balance, the router sends most tokens to a few experts. The paper adds an auxiliary loss (Section 2.2, Equations 4 to 6):

$$\text{loss} = \alpha \cdot N \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{N} f_i \cdot P_i$$

where $f_i$ is the fraction of tokens whose top-1 choice is expert $i$, and $P_i$ is the mean router probability for expert $i$.

Write two functions. Both take `p`, the `(T, N)` matrix of router probabilities $p_i(x)$.

- `expert_fractions(p)` returns `(f, P)`, each of shape `(N,)`.
- `load_balancing_loss(p, alpha=1e-2)` returns the scalar loss.
hints: $f_i$ counts hard assignments: take the argmax of each row first. It is the part that has no gradient.
$P_i$ is the plain mean of column $i$ of `p`. It is the part that carries the gradient to the router.
Both $f$ and $P$ sum to 1. With uniform routing, $\sum_i f_i P_i = N \cdot (1/N)(1/N) = 1/N$, which is why the loss multiplies by $N$.
